study_identification_part.si4_title: GPT- based normative models of brain sMRI correlate with dimensional psychopathology

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction clearly state the goal of investigating whether a GPT-based normative architecture applied to brain sMRI in youths can detect psychiatric symptoms and disorders, and specify the targeted datasets and outcomes (CBCL groups, ADHD scores, ASD diagnosis). This directly maps to the item’s criteria about research objectives and purpose of normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Here, we investigate whether a GPT- based normative architecture can detect psychiatric symptoms and disorders from brain sMRI of youths."; "We assess each brain Region of Interest (ROI) ... for associations with the CBCL groups of symptoms, ADHD scores, and diagnostics of ASD."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: They state models are trained exclusively on typically developing (TD) subjects and describe discarding subjects missing psychiatric evaluation, age, or sex. They also detail ABCD splits and the use of CBCL quartiles to assign examples to train/validation/test. However, explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria for TD status and image quality standards are not fully described, and reasons for exclusion beyond missing information are not detailed.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "our approach is normative as we use only typical subjects (i.e., normal) to train the models"; "Subjects with no information on psychiatric evaluation (i.e., ADHD, ASD, CBCL, or TD), age, or sex, were discarded."; "The subjects of ABCD were split into three sets for training (n=6,756), validation (n=751), and testing (n=3,524)..."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are summarized in demographics. They analyze age as a potential confounder by testing correlations with typicality scores. However, the normative model does not explicitly include age, sex, or site as covariates, and scanner/site effects are acknowledged as uncontrolled limitations.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "The likelihood of typicality was also used to assess the brain aging as a potential confounder..."; "our method does not control for the effect of scanners models"

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: They list all datasets (ABCD, BHRCS, ABIDE-II, ADHD-200), specify which are public or require authorization, and provide repository/URL references for acquisition parameters and access.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The datasets used in this study were obtained from two public datasets: the ABIDE-II and ADHD-200; and from two datasets that required authorization: ABCD and BHRCS... Detailed information... can be retrieved from ABIDE-II..., ADHD-200..., ABCD..., and BHRCS..."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: They use secondary datasets and refer readers to dataset documentation for acquisition parameters; per the guide, secondary data acquisition protocol should be marked NA.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "Detailed information on these datasets and their acquisition parameters can be retrieved from..."; "The data from ABCD were collected from 21 sites ... The BHRCS data were obtained ... 1.5T scanners..."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: They specify preprocessing software (SPM12), the VBM pipeline and a reference guide, voxel size resampling (1 mm^3), and that GM/WM were used. However, explicit quality control procedures are not described.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "The collected sMRI were preprocessed using the Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM)..."; "The VBM preprocessing ... was done through the Statistical Parametric Mapping software (SPM, version 12 release 7771)... parameters followed the SPM standard configuration pipeline ... with voxels' size set to 1 mm3..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They partition ABCD into training, validation, and testing sets and evaluate on reserved test data only, satisfying internal validation with held-out testing.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "the ABCD dataset was split into test and training/validation sets"; "The subjects of ABCD were split into three sets for training (n=6,756), validation (n=751), and testing (n=3,524)..."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: Out-of-sample datasets (ABIDE-II, ADHD-200, BHRCS) were fully reserved for the test phase and used for external evaluation.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "out-of-sample datasets were fully reserved for the test phase"; "The ABCD test set ... and the complete datasets of ABIDE-II, ADHD-200, and BHRCS were reserved for the evaluation procedure"

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: They describe the normative modeling framework using VQ-VAE and GPT, including that models are trained on TD subjects only; they provide architecture description, ensemble of nine GPTs, 50 training epochs, and a public code repository.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "architecture is composed of two models, a VQ-VAE ... and a GPT ..."; "our approach is normative as we use only typical subjects ... to train the models"; "we had nine GPT models ... predictions ... averaged in an ensemble ... number of training epochs was set to 50 ..."; "All source codes are publicly available (https://github.com/SergioLeonardoMendes/normative_psychiatry)"

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: While they report association metrics on held-out and external datasets (correlations and AUC), they do not provide quantitative fit/calibration metrics specifically for the reference cohort used to train the normative model (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, or coverage of intervals on training/validation partitions).
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Evaluation focuses on correlations with CBCL/ADHD scores and AUC for ASD on test datasets; no explicit model fit metrics for the reference cohort are reported.

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: They report ABCD training/validation/test sample sizes, but do not provide demographic characteristics per partition. Overall demographics are presented per dataset (Table 1) without partition-level breakdown.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: They specify preprocessing software and version (SPM12 v7771), programming environment (Python 3.8, PyTorch 1.12.0 with NVIDIA NGC 22.03), provide hardware details, and share a public code repository.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "The sMRI preprocessing was done through the SPM12 v7771 software... All further steps used Python 3.8 and Pytorch 1.12.0 ... The experiments were performed from an NVIDIA DGX-2 ..."; "All source codes are publicly available (https://github.com/SergioLeonardoMendes/normative_psychiatry)"

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses relate typicality likelihoods to clinical measures (CBCL, ADHD scores, ASD diagnosis) but do not model or adjust for additional clinical covariates such as medication status, illness duration, or comorbidities.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: Evaluation plan lists targets and metrics without additional covariates beyond the measured outcomes; no mention of medication status or similar variables.

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: They report per-dataset sample sizes, age, sex percentages, and CBCL total (where applicable). Clinical characteristics such as medication status or illness duration are not reported.

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: They specify clinical measures: CBCL symptom groups, ADHD symptom scores (inattention, hyperactivity/impulsivity, ADHD index), and ASD diagnosis; assessment procedures are briefly described for CBCL but not in procedural detail for all measures.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "These symptoms were measured by the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL) ... categories ... internalizing and externalizing ..."; "ADHD symptom groups include: inattention, hyperactivity/impulsivity, and ADHDindex scores."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: They define and use the "likelihood of typicality" derived from the GPT to indicate deviation from typical neuroanatomy and analyze associations with clinical measures. They do not provide explicit thresholds to categorize deviations (e.g., |Z|>1.96) but discuss relationships and limitations (e.g., scanner effects, age confounding).
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "our approach is normative ... atypicality is detected as a deviation from the learned pattern of typicality"; "we can ... obtain the map of likelihoods of typicality (per voxel) ..."; "The likelihood of typicality was also used to assess the brain aging as a potential confounder..."
